cohort: The study included 86,980 live-born singletons from the Danish National Birth Cohort.
finding: Maternal fever exposure during pregnancy was not associated with reduced head circumference, increased risk of microcephaly, or severe microcephaly in the offspring.
gest_age: Gestational age was used to define microcephaly (head circumference less than or equal to third percentile for sex and gestational age) and severe microcephaly (less than or equal to first percentile for sex and gestational age).
